prompt: Break a span down two ways: Period.between for calendar years/months/days, ChronoUnit.DAYS for the raw day count, and Duration for hours plus leftover minutes.
explanation: Period measures in calendar units and walks month by month, so Jan 31 to Mar 5 is "1 month and 5 days" -- the month step lands on Feb 29 because February has no 31st. ChronoUnit.DAYS ignores the calendar entirely and counts 34 real days for the same span, which is why the two answers look nothing alike. Duration works on exact time rather than dates: toHours() gives the whole span in hours while toMinutesPart() gives only the minutes left over, so the two together never double-count.
hints: Period.between(from, to) hands back an object with getYears(), getMonths() and getDays() -- those three parts add up to the span, they are not three separate totals.
ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(from, to) needs the import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit.
For the duration use toHours() for the first number but toMinutesPart() for the second; toMinutes() would give the whole span in minutes and print 1590 instead of 30.
